newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish police arrest six in border arms haul.
newsitem.headline: Irish police arrest six in border arms haul.

text.p: Irish police arrested six men and seized weapons and bomb components during a raid on Sunday in a remote area near the border with the British province of Northern Ireland.
A spokeswoman said they were being held in three police offices close to the arrest scene in the north-west County of Donegal.
Two AK-47 rifles, explosives and some mortar parts were found in a police swoop in the early hours.
Officers, who were said to have been on a routine patrol, became suspicious when they saw light in a shed near the village of Malin.
The district is some 20 miles (30 kms) from the border with County Londonderry in Northern Ireland.
Several arms caches belonging to the outlawed Irish Republican Army (IRA) have been uncovered in County Donegal and neighbouring southern counties in recent years.
The IRA, fighting to end British rule, ended a 17-month truce in February with bombs on mainland Britain.
It struck in Northern Ireland for the first time in two years on Octber 7, setting off car bombs that killed a soldier at British military headquarters at Lisburn, south of Belfast.
